title: The Clean Meat Directory
sub: 10 safe chicken brands to buy today
desc: Your 'organic' chicken might be bathed in chlorine. These ten air-chilled, pasture-raised brands do it differently, with where to buy each one.
text: Inside: 10 chicken brands we checked ourselves, where to buy each one, a store-by-store cheat sheet, and a four-step test for any brand not on this list. The dirty truth about "clean" chicken Walk into any grocery store and the chicken labels are covered in comforting words. Organic. Natural. Hormone-free. Humanely raised. What the labels almost never mention is what happened to that chicken after it was slaughtered. Most chicken sold in America is cooled in a giant shared tank of cold water. That water is treated with chlorine or other germ-killing chemicals, because thousands of birds are sitting in it together. This is called water-chilling . It is fast and cheap, which is why almost everyone does it. Here is the problem. While your chicken sits in that tank, it soaks up water (which you then pay for by the pound), it soaks up chemical residue, and it shares a bath with every other bird that went through that day. There is another way. Air-chilling cools each bird on its own, in a cold room, with no water at all. It takes longer and costs more, so most big producers skip it. But you get chicken with no added water, no chemical bath, and noticeably better texture when you cook it. The one word to look for If the package does not say "air-chilled" , assume the chicken was water-chilled with chemicals. "Natural", "organic", and even "no antibiotics ever" tell you nothing about how the bird was cooled. Look for the words air-chilled on the front of the pack. [Link a specific product here, e.g. the 10" skillet.] Shop NOTOXCHEF We did the checking so you can skip the detective work. Every brand below meets three tests: air-chilled processing, birds raised on pasture or genuinely free-range, and a company that is open about how it works. The 10 brands 1. Bell & Evans Air-chilled No antibiotics ever Humanely raised Bell & Evans has been air-chilling chicken since the 1990s, long before most shoppers knew the difference. Their birds are raised on family farms in Pennsylvania with access to sunlight and outdoor space, eat an all-vegetable diet, and are processed in the company's own facilities. Where to buy: Whole Foods, Wegmans, ShopRite, Stop & Shop, Giant, and most natural food stores. Also direct at bellandevans.com . 2. Mary's Free Range Air-chilled Free range Organic options Mary's chickens roam California farms with plenty of outdoor access. They sell both a standard and a certified organic line, and every bird is air-chilled. If you want to go further, their heritage-breed birds have flavour most people have never tasted from supermarket chicken. Where to buy: Whole Foods, Sprouts, Bristol Farms, Erewhon, and natural grocers across the West Coast. Expanding nationally through specialty retailers. 3. White Oak Pastures Air-chilled Pasture-raised Regenerative farm White Oak Pastures runs a zero-waste regenerative farm in Bluffton, Georgia. Chickens live on open pasture alongside cattle, moving from field to field. The farm processes birds on-site in its own USDA-inspected facility using air-chilling. This is about as close to your great-grandparents' chicken as you can get. Where to buy: Whole Foods (Southeast), or direct from whiteoakpastures.com with nationwide shipping. Use code LIFEUNTOX for a discount. 4. Cooks Venture Air-chilled Pasture-raised Heritage breed Cooks Venture raises its own slow-growing Pioneer breed on regenerative pasture in Arkansas. Slow-growing birds develop richer flavour than the fast-growing breeds used by big producers. All processing is air-chilled at their own facility, and they control every step from hatchery to package. Where to buy: Direct from cooksventure.com with nationwide shipping. Select Whole Foods locations. Also through the ButcherBox subscription. 5. Pasturebird Air-chilled Pasture-raised Moved daily Pasturebird moves its chickens to fresh grass every single day using mobile shelters, so the birds always have new pasture, bugs, and sunshine. Based in Southern California, they have managed to scale pasture-raised chicken without dropping their air-chilled standard. Where to buy: Erewhon, Bristol Farms, Lazy Acres, and select California retailers. Direct shipping via pasturebird.com . 6. Vital Farms Air-chilled Pasture-raised Certified Humane Vital Farms built its name on pasture-raised eggs and applies the same standard to chicken. Birds are raised on partner farms with at least 108 square feet of outdoor pasture each, far more than organic rules require. All processing is air-chilled. Where to buy: Whole Foods, Sprouts, Target (select locations), Kroger, Publix, and most major chains with a natural section. 7. Farmer Focus Air-chilled Certified organic Farmer-owned Farmer Focus is owned by the farmers who raise the birds, which keeps welfare standards high and the whole operation open to scrutiny. Based in Virginia's Shenandoah Valley, they sell both organic and humanely raised lines, all air-chilled. Their website lets you trace your chicken back to the exact farm it came from. Where to buy: Whole Foods, Wegmans, Harris Teeter, Publix, and growing availability on the East Coast. Direct shipping via farmerfocus.com . 8. Joyce Farms Air-chilled Free range Heritage breeds Joyce Farms in North Carolina specialises in heritage poultry, including their well-known Poulet Rouge. These slow-growing birds taste closer to what you would find in France than in a US supermarket, and every one is air-chilled. This is the brand chefs seek out. Where to buy: Direct from joyce-farms.com , select Whole Foods, and specialty butchers. 9. Shenandoah Valley Organic Air-chilled USDA organic 100% traceable Raised on small family farms in Virginia with outdoor access and certified organic feed. What sets them apart from bigger organic brands is that they did not cut the corner on processing: everything is air-chilled, and every pack can be traced from farm to fork. Where to buy: Whole Foods, MOM's Organic Market, and specialty grocers across the Mid-Atlantic. 10. Perdue Harvestland (organic air-chilled line) Air-chilled USDA organic Widely available This is the one for people who cannot get to a Whole Foods. Perdue's Harvestland organic air-chilled line brings clean chicken to mainstream stores at mainstream prices. Be careful here: Perdue also sells water-chilled chicken, so check the pack says air-chilled before it goes in the cart. Where to buy: Walmart, Costco, Kroger, Safeway, and most major chains nationwide. The most accessible option on this list. Quick reference: where to shop Store Clean brands available Whole Foods Bell & Evans, Mary's, Vital Farms, Farmer Focus, Joyce Farms Wegmans Bell & Evans, Farmer Focus Sprouts Mary's Free Range, Vital Farms Target Vital Farms (select locations) Walmart / Costco Perdue Harvestland Organic Air-Chilled Online direct White Oak Pastures, Cooks Venture, Pasturebird, Joyce Farms How to check any brand yourself Shopping somewhere that stocks none of these? Use this four-step test. Look for "air-chilled" on the front of the pack. This is the single most important thing. No air-chilled label means water-chilled with chemicals. Check for a third-party stamp. Certified Humane, Animal Welfare Approved, and Global Animal Partnership ratings mean someone outside the company checked the farm. Read the brand's website. Companies that are proud of their process talk about it openly. If you cannot find how they chill their birds, there is usually a reason. Watch the pan. Water-chilled chicken leaks liquid as it cooks and steams instead of browning. Air-chilled chicken holds its weight and gets golden. You just chose better chicken. Cook it in a better pan. Non-stick coatings can shed PFAS at the exact temperatures you sear chicken. NOTOXCHEF, our official cookware partner, only sells pans that pass the Lifeuntox Standard.
